title: The Sigil of the Ninefold Court
premise: Rosalind Villalobos has spent a lifetime keeping the Thornfell gate sealed and their own history buried, until prayers begin reaching the old gods and the Ninefold Court stirs beneath the mountain. When Rosalind learns that the soul of Wren, the foundling smuggler they raised as kin, was sold to the Court years ago by the very family Rosalind once served, they must lead a ragged band through every hidden road they know to steal that soul back before the Court's tithe-night seals it forever. The journey forces Rosalind to choose between the loyalty of the family they built and the truth of what they did to survive, culminating in a bargain where Rosalind offers their own memories as ransom. In the end Wren is freed, but Rosalind forgets them entirely—until Wren chooses to stay and rebuild those memories from scratch, proving that family is made twice: once by blood or choice, and again by devotion.
about_author: Hazel Thackeray grew up in a mining town ringed by hills she still insists are haunted, and her fiction braids folk horror with fierce tenderness for outsiders. She writes at night, after shifts, and credits her survival—and her stories—to the makeshift families she found along the way.

chapters.title: The Gate That Answers
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. On a routine patrol of the Thornfell gate, Rosalind hears a prayer pass through the stone—the first in forty years—and feels the old wards shiver awake. They dismiss it as mountain-madness, but that night a smuggler's child goes missing near the seal. Emotional beat: unease; the safe, invisible life is cracking.

chapters.title: Wren's Debt
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, now a grown smuggler with Rosalind's maps memorized, discovers a brand on their own shoulder burning hot whenever they cross the gate—a mark they've carried since infancy but never understood. A dying hedge-priest tells them it's a claim-mark of the Court below. Emotional beat: dread and denial.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Owes
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind descends to the archive beneath the shrine and finds the contract: Wren's soul, sold at birth by the Aldermarch family Rosalind once served, due for collection on tithe-night, six weeks away. Rosalind burns the copy—but the Court already knows. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a drowned thing.

chapters.title: A Family of Strays
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, mostly Wren's POV. Wren gathers their crew—Brannic the disgraced knight, Sefa the debt-witch, and Pip the lockchild—and tells them the truth. Each has a reason to refuse; each stays anyway. Emotional beat: warmth against fear; the found family formally binds itself.

chapters.title: Nine Roads Down
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The crew takes the first smuggler's road into the deep ways, navigating trials set by the waking old gods who test each traveler's oldest lie. Brannic nearly dies confessing his desertion. Emotional beat: rising tension; trust forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Tithe-Market
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. In an underground market where memories and names are currency, the crew trades pieces of themselves for passage and intelligence about the Court's vault. Sefa secretly pays with a memory of Wren, hiding the loss. Emotional beat: bittersweet sacrifice; the cost becomes real.

chapters.title: The Villalobos Confession
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, framed as a night-watch confession to Wren. Rosalind admits they witnessed the sale decades ago and stayed silent to keep their position—and Wren alive. Wren walks away furious. Emotional beat: the loyalty-vs-truth theme at its sharpest fracture.

chapters.title: Tithe-Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The Court opens its doors for the collection; the crew infiltrates amid the procession of claimed souls. Pip picks the vault, Brannic holds the door, Sefa unravels the ward—but the Ninefold sovereigns appear, and they know Rosalind by name. Emotional beat: climax begins; everything on the line.

chapters.title: The Ransom of Memory
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Cornered, Rosalind offers the one payment the Court values above souls: a keeper's unbroken memory, forty years of the gate's secrets, in exchange for voiding Wren's contract. The sovereigns accept. Wren screams no as Rosalind begins to forget. Emotional beat: devastating sacrifice, love made literal.

chapters.title: Learning You Again
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, months later. Above ground, the gate stands guarded by the whole crew, the old gods appeased. Rosalind remembers roads and duty but not Wren's face. Wren stays anyway, telling stories daily, planting new memories beside the empty space. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; found family chosen a second time.
